note: Resync wave (terminal output scheduler) of the module first harvested at 143c36e (src/renderer/src/lib/pane-manager/pane-terminal-output-scheduler.ts) to upstream v1.4.200. Between the pin and f352b6b, upstream sliced that ~1.1k-line file down to a 107-line re-export facade and moved its logic into a dozen pane-manager modules (pane-terminal-output-{pipeline,queue-backlog,queue-chunks,queue-registry,drain,writer,flusher,ack-credit,scheduler-debug}.ts, pane-terminal-foreground-{queue-state,render-settle}.ts, pane-terminal-cursor-sequencing.ts). Nexus did not mirror that split: this wave ports the three behavior fixes that land in those files and apply to Nexus's adapted single-file API, not the file layout. `upstreamUrl` below points to pane-terminal-output-queue-chunks.ts, the successor file carrying two of the three fixes; the third (the hold/coalesce release-deadline fix) predates the split and is cited by its original commit in changeSummary. Entries with `supersedes` replace the same nexusPath in orca-143c36e.json, whose entries are marked superseded. Not ported: the ack-credit/delivery-credit system (pane-terminal-output-ack-credit.ts — remote PTY multiplex flow control; different leva/worktree, no Nexus equivalent to extend) and the xterm `_core` dirty-row repaint optimization (orca#18169, pane-terminal-foreground-render-settle.ts — Nexus's header already excludes the private `_core` API this depends on). The mechanical split commits themselves (#16775, #17131) carried no behavior change and were not ported.

files.changeSummary: Ported three upstream behavior fixes onto the existing adapted API (state machine kept; no Orca file-split copied): (1) orca#8754 (d64ccc71b, pre-split pane-terminal-output-scheduler.ts) — hold/coalesce foreground timers cancelled each other's fallback forever on an alternating stream (a continuously repainting TUI), freezing a visible pane; ported as a shared foregroundReleaseDeadlineAt/Fixed gate (armForegroundReleaseDeadline/clearForegroundRelease) that caps one non-drainable episode regardless of how many times the mode flips. (2) orca#13402 / STA-3567 (868bfbe8c, pre-split) — partial takeQueuedChunk slices and drained queue slots kept V8's full parent string alive (e.g. a 2MB backlog chunk pinned by one un-flattened residual slice); ported flattenRetainedSlice with the same geometric re-flatten bound (residual <= retainedChars/2) plus clearing drained full-consume slots before the 64-chunk compaction. (3) perf (906bf54cc) — takeQueuedChunk assembled output via repeated `data +=`, quadratic across many small queued chunks (background floods, single-char writes); ported array+join assembly, kept our own ANSI-safe safeOutputSplitIndex chunking (upstream's post-split version does not have an equivalent — Nexus's split-avoidance is a deliberate divergence, not an omission).

secondaryProvenance.note: Carries the orca#8754 release-deadline gate at the pin (armForegroundReleaseDeadline / foregroundReleaseDeadlineFixed); fix 1 was ported from here, fixes 2 and 3 from the primary upstreamUrl (pane-terminal-output-queue-chunks.ts).

files.changeSummary: Added regression coverage for the three ported fixes, written against Nexus's own public API (writeTerminalOutput/flushTerminalOutput/getQueuedChars), not copied from any single upstream test file: a hold/coalesce alternation test proving the entry still becomes drainable (orca#8754), a many-small-chunks-in-order assembly test (906bf54cc's test adapted from enqueueChunk/takeQueuedChunk-level to public-API level since those are not exported here), a large-single-chunk-many-partial-takes content-integrity test for the retainedChars bookkeeping, and a flattenRetainedSlice content-preservation unit test. Upstream's STA-3567 heap-measurement tests (global.gc / --expose-gc) were deliberately NOT ported — see changeSummary note in this ledger's top-level `note` and the resync handoff summary.
